3_description:
new from-scratch family `models_r2/r2s3_null_supply`
  (worktree `worktrees/r2s3_lf_train_signal/B2`), condition-only at test,
  stripped view only, no LF tensor constructed on any test path.
  - `NullSupplyDecoder(cond_dim, width=64, blocks=4)`,
    `forward(cond, out_hw) -> (B,H,W)`; coord channels at forward time; lift
    2→64; 4× [SpectralConv2d(α) + 1×1 conv + FiLM(cond) after GroupNorm +
    GELU]; projection 64→128→1; FFT `norm="forward"`.
  - **Mode policy `pinned_min_rung_nyquist`** (E3b bug fix, MG-TFNO):
    `α = min(12, min over ALL train rungs of floor(N_rung/2))`, computed once
    per dataset and identical in every arm → ifc_poisson α = 4 (rungs
    8/16/32/64), cahn_hilliard and fisher_kpp α = 12 (rungs 64/128/256). No
    mode weight is ever supervised by the 5 HF rows alone.
  - **Per-rung scaler** `s_f = max|y|` on rung `f`'s own train fields (E3a,
    declared as an amplitude-convention fix, not a claim); the HF scaler is
    therefore identical across arms (closes B1's C1).
  - **Step-matched budget** (closes B1's C2): `steps = --epochs × 25`
    (200 → 5000; contract 2 → 50); every arm takes the same steps, sees all 5
    HF rows every step, same AdamW(1e-3, wd 1e-5) + cosine + clip 1.0. LF arms
    additionally draw one 16-row LF minibatch per step (rungs cycled
    deterministically).
  - **Loss** `MSE_HF + 1.0·MSE_LF + 1.0·NullPenalty` in per-rung-scaled units.
    `NullPenalty` = paired-difference penalty along the HF design's null
    directions: sample `c` from the train conditions, `v ∈ null([X_hf,1])`,
    `t ~ U(−1,1)` (standardized units), penalize
    `‖[S(c+tv) − S(c)] − t·(vᵀΘ_LF)‖²`, where `Θ_LF` is a ridge-affine law on
    the LF rung selected by that rung's own in-rung LOO, lifted to the HF grid
    with the ADR r2-0001 convention (imported read-only / vendored with a 1e-9
    train-split agreement assert). `m = dim null = 0` ⇒ penalty ≡ 0 by
    construction.
  - **N_hf = 5 protocol**: native on ifc_poisson; on the two aligned datasets
    5 of the existing 400 train HF rows are drawn by `R2S3B2_SPLIT_SEED` while
    the LF rungs keep all 400 conditions (LF at 395 conditions with no HF row).
    Training-free null deficit at N_hf = 5: `m` = 1 (ifc, d=5), **15**
    (cahn_hilliard, d=19), **0** (fisher_kpp, d=2).
  - **Arms** (each with its own `ROUND2_EVAL_RESULTS` dir ⇒ own `ckpt_dir`
    and cache key):

    | arm | LF pool | null penalty | dataset(split seeds) |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | `A0_nolf` | — | off | ifc(native), ch(0,1,2), fk(0,1) |
    | `A1_lf_cov` | all rungs, all conditions | off | ifc(native), ch(0) |
    | `A2_lf_cov_null` **PRIMARY** | all rungs, all conditions | on | ifc(native), ch(0,1,2), fk(0,1) |
    | `A3_lf_paired` | LF at the 5 HF conditions only | vacuous | ch(0) |
    | `A5_lf_norepair` | all rungs (B1 config: shared `max|y|`, unpinned modes) | off | ifc(native) |

    On fisher_kpp `m = 0` ⇒ `A2 ≡ A1`; only `A2` is run and the identity is
    recorded.
  - **Non-trained reference splits** (never named `test*`): `ref_linear_mf`
    (the preempted channel `c·A(cond)+R(cond)`, rung by in-rung LOO, `c` and
    residual ridge on the 5 HF rows, α by exact LOO), `ref_linear_hfonly`
    (min-norm affine = the information limit), and the floor arms `ref_zero`,
    `ref_train_mean_n5`, `ref_nn_condition_n5` (in-regime) plus
    `ref_train_mean_full` / `ref_nn_condition_full` seam-checked to
    `state/anchors/floors.json` at 1e-9, RAISING on mismatch.
  - **Reported gate/instrument block** (E4 — reported, never a switch):
    per-rung affine-LOO residual, `m`, singular values of `[X_hf,1]`,
    null-direction energy fraction, LF→null recovery cosine/gain, per-arm
    train-vs-test gap, and predictions dumped at the HF **train** conditions
    (B1 part 7 item (4)).
  - **Declared baseline** (§12.3): `mf_fno_transfer_film`, **cited** from B1's
    on-disk gate run — ifc_poisson, 200 epochs, seed 0, nRMSE **0.055637**,
    skill **1.5455**, `nrmse_def_hash d3d0ade9… / copylf_def_hash 9753ff24…`
    (`…/round2/r2s3_lf_train_signal/B1/eval/result_ifc_poisson_baseline_mf_fno_transfer_film_s0.json`);
    ifc_poisson's native N_hf is 5, so it is exactly regime-matched. Stated
    differences: joint step-matched training with per-rung scalers, pinned
    modes and a null-direction penalty vs sequential LF-pretrain→HF-finetune
    with no null-space machinery. Not re-run, not edited.
  - **Guard leg**: `A2` on `--datasets guard`, contract tier (2 epochs), native
    N_hf (`R2S3B2_GUARD_NSUB=off`).
4_expected_result:
(skill units, corrected denominators, seed 0,
  `provisional-single-seed`):

  | quantity | prediction | vs floor / anchor |
  |---|---|---|
  | ifc `A0_nolf` | 8–12 (best est. 9.5) | B1's `hf_only` 9.4466; NN floor 10.054891 |
  | ifc `A2_lf_cov_null` (PRIMARY) | **2–8** (best est. 5) | information limit 3.4744; declared baseline 1.5455; preempted linear channel 0.2427 |
  | **ifc value-of-LF `A0 − A2`** | **+2 to +7** (best est. +4.5) | certified mce **0.9377041** → **2.1–7.5× the floor**; B1 measured **−7.3497** |
  | ifc `A5_lf_norepair − A2` | +5 to +12 | prices the repair trio in-job vs 0.9377041 |
  | cahn_hilliard `A0` (mean of 3 draws, N_hf=5) | 25–45 | frozen 400-row NN floor 23.180342; in-regime N=5 floors reported beside it |
  | cahn_hilliard `A0 − A2` | **+1 to +8** | vs `max(0.0912454, in-job paired spread over 3 draws)` → ≥ 11× the floor |
  | cahn_hilliard `A3_lf_paired − A2` | +0.5 to +5 | coverage beyond curriculum, same threshold |
  | fisher_kpp `A0 − A2` (mean of 2 draws) | −0.5 to +0.5 | predicted **null**; must sit below cahn_hilliard's effect (raw effect also reported vs `max(0.0007137, in-job spread)`) |
  | panel geomean | **not computed** | 3 of 6 panel datasets scored; no criterion-2 panel claim; stream anchor 23.063617 quoted for context only |

  Why the ifc sign should flip: the null direction carries 18.83% of the law's
  coefficient energy and the LF rungs recover it at 0.940/0.982/0.996 (B1 turn
  2 B7); per-rung scaling removes the 1772× HF-loss deflation B1's part 6
  blames for the row-space damage (0.921 vs the control's 0.604); pinned modes
  remove the `|k|>4` band that only 5 deflated rows supervised (+1.605 post
  hoc); the null penalty caps the 2.653× gain error. The card does **not**
  predict beating the declared baseline (1.5455) or the preempted linear
  channel (0.2427) — the deliverable is the certified measurement, not a
  champion. Standing caveat carried: ifc_poisson is an exactly affine benchmark
  (affine-LOO 3.2e-08), so any bar-level number there is **rank recovery, not
  operator learning** (B1 part 6 M11). helmholtz and pfc are not scored, so
  their standing caveats do not arise on this card.

interpretation: M1 (high confidence; turns 1-3 jointly) - THE THREE-CHANNEL DECOMPOSITION OF THE VALUE OF LF. LF rows at conditions carrying no HF row help a condition->field surrogate through three mechanically distinct channels, and which one dominates is set by the dataset's deficit structure, not by any property of the LF fields: (i) DIRECTION SUPPLY - the LF rows carry the component of the true law that the HF design's null space hides (ifc_poisson: recovered at cos +0.9995, ratio 1.019; 57-60% of the effect); (ii) ROW-SPACE FIT - a better estimate of the directions the HF rows DO determine (ifc: 2.17x lower law error, ~40% of the effect; cahn_hilliard: 2.9x, rel-L2 1.14 -> 0.39); (iii) LEVEL / AMPLITUDE VARIANCE REDUCTION - a Monte-Carlo-better estimate of the response's scale, which is the ENTIRE effect when m = 0 (fisher_kpp: 77% level, LF level interchangeable with the true 400-row HF level) and re-appears at m = 15 as amplitude control of the null block (cahn_hilliard: 2.1-2.7x over-amplitude and anti-aligned without LF, 0.89-0.99 with it). Channel (iii) is a SAMPLE-SIZE mechanism, reproducible by any 400-row estimate of the same statistic; only (i) is information the HF rows could never contain. Reporting 'the value of LF' as one number therefore conflates an identifiability fix with a variance-reduction trick.

M2 (high confidence; turn 3 T3.5/T3.6) - AND THE STRONG READING OF (i) IS DATASET-SPECIFIC. On ifc_poisson - exactly affine, m = 1 - LF genuinely supplies the missing direction. On cahn_hilliard the LF arms reach only cos +0.05...+0.22 in the unseeable block: they do not teach the direction, they stop the model inventing a large wrong one, and the null family is no better than a random 15-d subspace at absorbing the error. The honest generalisation across the panel is 'LF coverage calibrates the amplitude/variance of the model's response in whatever subspace the HF rows do not constrain'; the identifiability story is a special case that needs an (almost) affine dataset to be visible.

M3 (high confidence; turn 3 T3.7/T3.8) - F3 IS ABOUT COVERAGE OF THE CONDITION DESIGN, NOT ABOUT LF FIELDS. Adding LF rows at conditions that already carry an HF row cannot change the augmented design's rank, null dimension or singular values (verified bit-identical), so a paired arm has zero access to the deficient subspace; and where the coarse solve is a genuinely different field (cahn_hilliard rung 1: rel-L2 0.398, one condition 1.398) those rows are a contradictory target on exactly the rows the HF loss supervises, which is why A3 lands 0.8276 BELOW the no-LF control. The transportable design rule for any MF training recipe: spend the LF budget on NEW conditions; LF at covered conditions is at best redundant and, on sharp/multistable PDEs, harmful.

M4 (high confidence; turn 1 + turn 2 T2.9) - THE CARD'S OWN HEADLINE MECHANISM IS THE ONLY NET-NEGATIVE INGREDIENT IT SHIPPED. The null-direction penalty is aimed correctly (cos +0.98-0.99) but calibrated to a target that is 1.72-1.79x too large because (a) the measured amplitude gain 0.5510075 was reported and not applied and (b) in_rung_loo broke a 1e-08 affinity tie toward the coarsest rung, whose lifted law systematically over-states the null coefficient (gain 0.551 -> 0.744 -> 0.919 monotone in rung fineness). Even a perfectly calibrated, perfectly rung-selected penalty (best counterfactual 2.6349) does not reach the penalty-free arm A1 (2.1690), because ~20% of the penalty's displacement is collateral row-space damage. The mechanism to keep is coverage; the penalty should be dropped, not retuned.

M5 (decision-relevant; high confidence on the numbers, medium on the framing) - WHAT B3 AND THE ROUND REPORT SHOULD DO WITH THE A1-NOT-A2 RESULT. The card's PRIMARY designation (A2_lf_cov_null) is not the card's best measurement of the value of LF: the simpler coverage arm A1_lf_cov wins on both datasets where both ran (ifc A0-A1 = 5.9654 vs 4.6794; cahn_hilliard A0-A1 = 17.4437 vs 16.7358), and the gap is attributable to the penalty (ifc 1.2860 = 1.37x floor; ch 0.7080 = 7.8x that dataset's floor). The claimable deliverable - round-2 success criterion 1 - is therefore the MATCHED BUDGET-EQUAL +-LF CONTRAST WITH THE COVERAGE ARM: A0_nolf vs A1_lf_cov, with A2 reported beside it as a pre-registered mechanism that failed. This costs nothing in novelty (the prior-art verdict's novel row E5 is the measurement, not the penalty) and removes the awkwardness of a primary arm that is beaten by its own ablation. A1 was run on only 2 of the 3 datasets (ifc, cahn_hilliard draw 0) and on 1 of the 3 cahn_hilliard draws, so B3's cheapest high-value leg is to complete A1 on the remaining draws and on fisher_kpp (where A2 == A1 identically, m = 0, so it is already complete) before the round-end 3-seed extension.

Every arm of this family emits a condition response carrying 77-92% of the truth's fluctuation energy at ~0.065 alignment, so a constant field beats all of them; A0 (no LF at all) loses to the same in-regime floor by MORE than A2 does (3.78/3.32 vs 2.09/2.57). 6_analysis.falsification_postmortem:
The four pre-registered clauses that could be decided came out CONFIRMED (F1 +4.6794 = 4.99x floor; F2 +32.8585; F3 +17.5633 vs an operative threshold of 4.8061; F4 ordering ch 14.2454 >> fk 1.2228), and F5 is ambiguous by wording. Mechanism-level, four things need to be said.

(1) F1's SIGN FLIP VS B1 IS AN ARCHITECTURE FIX CONFIRMING AN INFORMATION CLAIM. B1 measured -7.3497 on the same dataset with the same LF rows and split the verdict: falsified as an ARCHITECTURE claim, correct as an INFORMATION claim (B1 part 6). B2 changed three instrument knobs (per-rung max|y| scalers, mode budget pinned to the coarsest rung's Nyquist, step-matched budget) and the same contrast is now +4.6794. Turn 1 shows the repair worked through the predicted route: B1's no-LF control put 27.7% of its law energy in the null direction at cos -0.9919 (wrong-way extrapolation), B2's A0_nolf puts 0.025% (std) / 16.1% (raw) there, and A5_lf_norepair - B1's configuration re-run in-job - reproduces B1's pathology (null ratio +2.90 vs B1's +2.653, skill 36.31, worse than the zero floor). So the information claim B1 could only make with a linear probe is now carried by a neural condition->field surrogate: LF rows at uncovered conditions are worth 4.7-6.0 skill units to a matched, budget-equal, normalization-matched network. Caveat carried unchanged from B1 part 6 (M11): ifc_poisson is affine to 3.2e-08, so any bar-level number there is rank recovery, not operator learning.

(2) F5's WORDING IS AMBIGUOUS AND BOTH READINGS MUST BE STATED. The clause ends '...or if A2 fails to beat its own in-regime N=5 best floor on both sharp datasets'. LITERAL reading ('fails on BOTH' = falsified only if it fails on both): NOT falsified, because cahn_hilliard passes on all three draws (12.83-13.34 vs ref_zero 23.9217). INTENT reading ('must beat the floor on both'): FALSIFIED, because fisher_kpp's A2 (15.2500 / 15.4341) loses to its own train_mean_n5 floor (13.1624 / 12.8658) by 2.09 / 2.57 skill units, ~2900x that dataset's min_claimable_effect. Turn 2 resolves what the miss MEANS even though it cannot resolve the wording: the fisher_kpp floor loss is a property of the task's condition vector shared by every condition-response arm on the card, not a defect of the LF signal. Every arm - with LF and without - emits a fluctuation field carrying 77-92% of the truth's fluctuation energy at pooled alignment 0.064-0.070 (per-sample cos ~0.05), which is pure added error; the optimal shrinkage of that channel is lambda* = 0.1 in all four legs. The no-LF control loses to the same floor by MORE (3.78 / 3.32). So under the intent reading F5 fires against the FAMILY on fisher_kpp (a deterministic condition->HF map there is bounded by the conditional-mean floor, ADR r2-0003), not against the card's LF claim; the +1.2228 m=0 LF effect and the floor miss are the same fact seen twice (turn 2 H7). The card should be read as: F5 confirmed on ifc_poisson and cahn_hilliard, and NOT ASSESSABLE as an LF claim on fisher_kpp.

(3) THE NULL PENALTY WAS A SELF-INFLICTED AMPLITUDE WOUND. The clauses do not mention it, but the card's own headline mechanism is the only ingredient that lost skill where it was active: A1 -> A2 costs 1.2860 on ifc (1.37x the certified floor) and 0.7080 on cahn_hilliard (7.8x that dataset's floor). Turn 1 shows why: the penalty's direction is right (cos +0.98-0.99 with the ORACLE) but its target amplitude is 1.72-1.79x too large - exactly 1/0.5510075, the gain the family measured, printed in the gate block as REPORTED_NOT_APPLIED, and then did not apply - and it was aimed at an arm whose null coefficient was ALREADY correct to 1.0-1.9% (A1 ratio +1.0185, cos +0.99947). 51.7% of the regression is canonically attributable to that one direction; the other ~48% is collateral (17.5-21.3% of the penalty's displacement lands in the row space; non-affinity doubles). Turn 2 adds the second half of the causal chain: the target came from the coarsest LF rung because in_rung_loo broke a 9.8e-09 affinity tie, and over-amplitude is monotone in rung coarseness (0.551/0.744/0.919), worth another 0.6397 (below the claimable floor on its own). The instrument-hygiene lesson: a gate quantity that is measured, printed and NOT applied is a live bug, and a regulariser aimed at a quantity the model already has right can only subtract.

(4) WHAT THE CARD ACTUALLY ESTABLISHES IS A THREE-CHANNEL DECOMPOSITION OF THE VALUE OF LF. F1/F3/F4 read as one sentence ('LF at uncovered conditions helps, LF at covered conditions does not, and the effect scales with the null deficit') understate the result. Across the three datasets the value decomposes into DIRECTION SUPPLY (ifc: 57-60% of the effect, cos +0.9995 - genuinely information the HF rows cannot contain), ROW-SPACE FIT (ifc ~40%, 2.17x lower law error; cahn_hilliard 2.9x), and LEVEL/AMPLITUDE VARIANCE REDUCTION (fisher_kpp: 77% of the effect and the LF level is interchangeable with the true 400-row HF level; cahn_hilliard: amplitude of the unseeable block 2.1-2.7x -> 0.89-0.99). Which channel dominates is set by the dataset's deficit structure - m = 0 and level-dominated (fisher_kpp) vs m = 15 and fluctuation-dominated (cahn_hilliard) vs m = 1 and exactly affine (ifc_poisson) - and the third channel is a sample-size effect that any 400-row estimator would reproduce. F4's confirmed ordering is therefore the coarse shadow of this: the null deficit predicts the SHARE of the effect that is information, not the size of the effect.
surprises: A3_lf_paired is WORSE than training with no LF at all (30.9058 vs 30.0783, 9.1x the dataset floor, on 65% of test samples). The card expected 'coverage beyond curriculum' (+0.5 to +5); the measured curriculum contribution is negative. Turn 3 explains it: the paired pool leaves the design's rank/null-dimension/singular values bit-identical, so it cannot help, and its rung-1 fields differ from HF by rel-L2 0.398 (one condition 1.398) at exactly the conditions the HF loss supervises, so it can hurt.

On cahn_hilliard the LF arms barely align with the truth in the 15 unseeable directions (Frobenius cos +0.05 to +0.22) yet capture 68% of the LF effect there - the value came from removing a 2.1-2.7x anti-aligned over-extrapolation, not from learning the right law. On ifc_poisson the same channel is a cos +0.9995 direction transfer. The mechanism labelled 'null-direction supply' in B1 and in this card's motivation is thus two different mechanisms wearing one name.

The card's part-4 prediction for fisher_kpp ('A0 - A2 in [-0.5, +0.5], predicted null') missed: the measured effect is +1.2228, 1713x the certified floor and above the 2-draw spread 0.9416. A dataset with ZERO null deficit still shows a resolvable LF benefit, because the level of a 5-row conditional-mean estimate is 0.119 wrong while the LF rung mean's HF bias is 0.004-0.014.

The LF rung-2 mean field is a marginally BETTER constant predictor of the fisher_kpp test set than the full 400-row HF train mean (11.99143 vs 11.99311), at zero HF cost - a training-free reminder that on level-dominated tasks the LF ladder can substitute for HF sampling outright.

A5_lf_norepair (B1's configuration, in-job) is worse than predicting zero (36.3135 vs the 27.7778 zero floor) - the un-repaired instrument does not merely fail to use LF, it is actively anti-informative. But it moves three knobs at once (scaler, mode policy, 8x parameter count), so it prices the repair BUNDLE and not any single repair (reviewer carry-forward, part 5 F2 caveat).
